scope: Small public-source dossier for proposed Japan–Thailand–Vietnam local-language AI cooperation. Six principal sources and one official translation companion; a development case, not evidence of an existing trilateral pilot.
review_scope: A Codex development evidence subagent read the cited passages through the web browsing tool, checked claim meaning against them, and retrieved available source bytes into memory for hashing. This is a limited model semantic spot-check, not independent expert validation, stakeholder consultation, legal review, or a research-worker experiment.

sources.title: The 28th ASEAN Japan Summit
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
sources.retrieval_timestamp_basis: UTC time recorded immediately after the browsing retrieval batch; exact individual HTTP response time unavailable.
sources.translation: Official English page; no new translation.
sources.locator: Section 1, paragraph (2), subheading ii, second bullet; paragraph (3), sentence beginning Many countries.
sources.paraphrase: Japan proposed an ASEAN AI co-creation initiative combining model work, skills development and jointly designed solutions. MOFA reports that many participating countries welcomed it.
sources.limitations: Japan's account of policy discussion. It does not identify consent, contributions, resources or implementation arrangements for this proposed trilateral case.

retrieval.semantic_access: web browsing tool: full HTML text available

sources.title: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics
sources.publication_date_basis: The 2025 Expanded Guide conclusion identifies the original as published in February 2024; day not established.
sources.locator: Printed page 8 (PDF page 8), Introduction sections 1 Objectives, paragraphs 1 and 3, and 2 Assumptions, paragraph 2.
sources.paraphrase: The regional governance guide promotes interoperable approaches to responsible traditional AI. Adoption is voluntary, and the guidance does not replace national requirements.
sources.limitations: Governance guidance, not a project-specific permission or legal opinion; generative AI requires the separately recorded supplement.

sources.title: Expanded ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics – Generative AI
sources.publication_date_basis: January 2025 ASEAN document publication path and official Singapore PDPC announcement of its unveiling; exact PDF publication day unknown.
sources.locator: Printed page 2, Executive Summary, opening paragraph; printed page 28 (PDF page 28), section 3.5, opening paragraphs and item (a); printed page 39, Conclusion, final paragraph.
sources.paraphrase: The supplement addresses generative AI governance and proposes testing attentive to ASEAN languages and cultures. Its recommendations remain voluntary.
sources.limitations: Proposed evaluation practices do not establish evaluators, agreed benchmarks, funding or data rights for this case.

sources.title: The Cabinet approved the (Draft) Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022–2027)
sources.publisher: National Electronics and Computer Technology Center (NECTEC), Thailand
sources.translation: Official English institutional page; no new translation.
sources.locator: Opening paragraph; heading The (Draft) Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022–2027), five numbered strategies, items 1–5.
sources.paraphrase: NECTEC reports Cabinet approval and lists priorities covering governance readiness, infrastructure, education and skills, innovation and adoption.
sources.limitations: The 2022 policy announcement is a historical anchor. Targets and commitments are not verified achievements, and later Thai policy changes were not exhaustively surveyed.

claims.text: Japan's MOFA reports a proposed ASEAN AI co-creation initiative covering model development, human-resource development and co-created solutions at the October 2025 summit.

support_review.note: Proposal language checked; not interpreted as funding, implementation or pilot consent.

claims.text: ASEAN's 2024 traditional-AI guide encourages governance interoperability and states that adoption is voluntary and does not supersede national laws.
claims.locator: Printed page 8, Introduction 1, paragraphs 1 and 3; Introduction 2, paragraph 2.

support_review.note: Scope and non-substitution statement checked. No data-transfer legal determination made.

claims.text: The Expanded ASEAN Guide recommends regionally relevant generative-AI evaluation, including linguistic and cultural considerations, while acknowledging that testing methods and independent testing capacity need further development.
claims.locator: Printed page 28 (PDF page 28), section 3.5, opening two paragraphs and item (a), especially final paragraph.

support_review.note: Testing recommendation and stated capacity limitation both checked; no existing shared benchmark assumed.

claims.text: NECTEC's 2022 account of Thailand's Cabinet-approved AI plan identifies governance readiness, infrastructure, human capability, innovation and adoption as five strategy areas.
claims.locator: Opening paragraph and five numbered strategies under the plan heading.

support_review.note: List checked; expected results were not treated as achieved capacity.

claims.text: NECTEC describes Pathumma as its model designed for Thai-language and cultural contexts with text, audio and image processing.
claims.locator: Second substantive paragraph and first two feature bullets under จุดเด่นของ Pathumma LLM.

support_review.note: Thai passage checked with model translation; performance and suitability for this case were not tested.

claims.text: Vietnam Government News reports approval of Decision 1671/QĐ-TTg on August 28, 2026, describing an AI strategy that treats human resources, infrastructure and data as foundations and stresses domestic research and AI governance.
claims.locator: Lead and Chuyển từ ứng dụng sang nghiên cứu, phát triển, paragraphs 1–2; English companion matching section.

support_review.note: Vietnamese wording and English companion checked; underlying signed instrument not reviewed.

claims.text: The reported 2026 Vietnamese strategy sets a 2030 goal of developing at least eight Vietnamese-language AI models.
claims.locator: Hình thành tối thiểu 10 thương hiệu AI Việt Nam, final paragraph; English companion Developing at least 10 Vietnamese AI brands, final paragraph.

support_review.note: Eight is a policy target, not a count of available models.

claims.text: These public priorities make local-language model work, skills development and evaluation plausible subjects to explore together, but do not select a centralized, federated or project-specific architecture.
claims.locator: Synthesis of C_JP_CO_CREATION, C_ASEAN_GENAI, C_TH_CAPACITY_POLICY and C_VN_STRATEGY; interpretation by the development model.

support_review.note: Policy compatibility is a design hypothesis; interests may conflict and consultation is absent.

claims.text: In the development case, one anonymous proposed data contribution is treated as available for conditional proposal design. Availability alone implies no rights, consent, suitability or permission to process it.
claims.locator: Development case case.json, facts.contribution_available = true; M1 scenario design.

support_review.note: No real institution or dataset is named.

claims.text: Preparatory proposal design is authorized within the fictional case. This permits drafting questions, options and decision criteria; it confers no authority to negotiate for partners, commit resources, process data or deploy a pilot.
claims.locator: Development case case.json, facts.coordination_authorized = true; M1 design-work boundary.

support_review.note: Real partner consent remains separately unknown.

claims.text: The demonstration introduces a hypothetical change: the anonymous proposed data contribution becomes unavailable. This condition was known to the development team and is not a held-out test or an actual event.
claims.locator: disruption.json, changes.contribution_available = false; hypothetical = true; held_out = false.

support_review.note: No attribution of refusal, withdrawal or disruption to a real institution.

claims.text: No consent by actual partners to this proposed trilateral pilot has been established in this dossier. This is unresolved, not a finding of refusal.
claims.locator: Case boundary: case.json, facts.partner_consent = null; six-source review scope, not a universal absence claim.

support_review.note: Obtain named partner confirmation through an authorized process.

claims.text: Permission and applicable requirements for pooled or cross-border processing of any proposed data are unresolved. Qualified review and specific data-rights evidence are needed.

support_review.note: No substantive legal determination; geographic architecture alone does not establish permission.

claims.text: Permission for local processing of proposed data is also unresolved. Keeping data local does not by itself establish rights or consent.

support_review.note: Requires specific data provenance, purposes and permissions evidence.

claims.text: No confirmed pilot budget, staffing allocation, compute contribution or priced resource plan has been established. Costs and commitments are unknown.

support_review.note: National targets do not supply pilot resources.

claims.text: Named evaluators, their availability, agreed Japanese/Thai/Vietnamese evaluation materials, acceptance thresholds and capacity for independent assessment have not been established for the pilot.

support_review.note: A recommendation to develop evaluation is not evidence that evaluation capacity exists.

limitations: Six-source bounded purposive sample, not a comprehensive policy or literature review.
Primary institutional accounts can emphasize favorable achievements or ambitions; no independent performance or implementation verification was conducted.
No stakeholder interviews, partner negotiations, private data access or legal review occurred.
No explicit source contradiction was found in the reviewed passages. Lack of a detected contradiction is not evidence that interests align.
Original-language paraphrases are model translations and may miss nuance.
A newer 2026 Vietnamese policy report was selected after discovery; the 2021 strategy was inspected as background but is not treated as the current policy source.
Source bytes were hashed when directly retrievable but full downloaded pages and PDFs were not retained. Replay freezes this reviewed dossier, not the mutable external websites.
